copies.headline: Adam's Kicker Never Showed, Isaac Did
copies.body:
The margin was 3.9 and the kicker slot was 10.3 to nothing. Will Reichard put up a zero, and in a game Adam lost by less than four points, that's the whole story — every other decisive edge canceled out. Adam won the backfield by 14.3 behind Bucky Irving's 21.0 and got 8.0 from the Patriots defense while Isaac's Colts managed 1.0, and it still wasn't enough, because Ja'Marr Chase's 31.1 and T.J. Hockenson's 15.8 swung receiver and tight end the other way.
Isaac shouldn't have been this close to clean. Javonte Williams went 6.7 on a 20.1 projection, Jakobi Meyers put up 4.4, and Dalton Kincaid sat on the bench with 18.6. He won anyway. Adam's own problems were quieter: Jayden Daniels 15.0 on 22.8, Kenneth Walker III 12.4 on 19.9, a third straight week under 110 for the league's top scorer at 139.6 per game.
We picked Adam by 21, which aged about as well as the kicker slot. Isaac now leads the reigning champ 5-3 all-time, still at 4-4 with a 31-57 all-play that says the ledger is coming due.

copies.headline: Burrow Buries Grant Before Zay Even Shows
copies.body:
Quarterback decided this one. Joe Burrow went for 39.5 and Kyler Murray answered with 19.9, a 19.6-point hole Grant was never built to climb out of — especially with Patrick Mahomes and his 25.4 points watching from the bench. Add Logan winning the backfield by nine on Braelon Allen and Jaylen Warren, and the 33.8-point margin was functionally settled by three starters.
Grant's actual killer was Zay Flowers: 20.1 projected, zero actual, a 20-point donut that by itself covers most of the gap. Tony Pollard's 28.7 and the Commanders defense's 14 were wasted effort. Logan won despite Tyler Higbee scoring 2.4, the Chiefs D/ST scoring 2.0, and Tyler Allgeier rotting on his bench with 36.1 — a reminder that he still doesn't need to be right to be ahead.
Logan's 4th-best scoring finally bought a win; at 3-5 with a 54-34 all-play, he's been the unluckiest team in the league. Our preview had Grant by 7. It did not age.

copies.headline: Penix Goes Negative, CJ Goes Nowhere
copies.body:
CJ lost this at quarterback before anything else happened. Michael Penix Jr. posted minus-1.9 against a 15.5 projection, a 17-point swing on one roster slot, and Trevor Lawrence's modest 19.4 was enough to turn that into a 21.3-point positional landslide. Add Bhayshul Tuten's 29.9 — more than CJ's entire backfield, where Jonathan Taylor managed 6.7 on a 15.6 projection — and the 28.4 margin was decided in two spots. Parker Washington's 3.6 on 16.0 was just piling on.
Christian won while his tight end scored 3.2, his defense scored 1.0, and CeeDee Lamb came in seven points under projection. That's what a 126.5 per-game offense looks like on an average day. Chuba Hubbard's 24.9 and the Steelers' 16.0 were real contributions; they were also the only ones.
Christian's to 4-5 with an all-play of 54-34, which says he's been the third-best team in this league and has the losing record to prove nothing. CJ drops to 4-4 and has now scored 90.9, 95.1 in back-to-back weeks. The preview had Christian by 12. Should have said more.

copies.headline: Josh Allen Drags a Corpse Across the Line
copies.body:
This was a quarterback game, which is the polite way of saying nobody else showed up. Josh Allen's 26.6 was more than Leif's entire non-Allen lineup except Derrick Henry, and it covered a 17.6-point edge at the position that Kaleb never came close to erasing. Kaleb got 23.4 from Harold Fannin Jr. and a tidy 20.8-point win at tight end, then watched Jared Goff miss projection by seven, Drake London miss by sixteen, and Breece Hall post a zero. Final margin: 1.9.
The actual killer was Tre Tucker's donut with Keenan Allen (13.7), Ladd McConkey (12.6), and Jordan Addison (11.6) all rotting on Kaleb's bench. Any of the three wins it going away. Leif wasn't blameless — Chris Godwin and Omar Cooper Jr. both zeroed on 10.6 projections — but 64.7 points beat 62.7, and that's the whole sport.
Leif is 6-2 with a 43-45 all-play and +2.1 luck wins; Joey Lunchbox is stealing a season in broad daylight. Our preview had Kaleb by seven, which aged roughly as well as his flex decisions.

copies.headline: Noah's Kicker And Defense Buried Mitchell
copies.body:
The skill positions were basically a tie. Mitchell lost QB by 2.7, RB by 3.3 and WR by 3.6, and actually won the flex by eight on Rachaad White. Then you get to the bottom of the lineup and the game is over: Tyler Loop 2.6 and the Bengals D/ST 2.0 against Chad Ryland 10.9 and the Jaguars' 21.0. That's 27.3 points of difference from the two roster spots nobody drafts on purpose, and it accounts for nearly all of a 34.6-point loss.
Jahmyr Gibbs (24.8) and Matthew Golden (20.9) did their jobs. Jordan Mason turning 9.5 projected into 2.0 did not, and Travis Kelce sat on the bench with 11.7 while Tyler Warren produced 5.8. Noah had his own mess — Hunter Henry at flex for 6.0 while Jaylen Waddle (14.9) and Josh Downs (12.3) watched — and it didn't matter, because Michael Wilson went for 26.8.
Mitchell falls to 1-7 with a 30-58 all-play, last in the league; the human coin flip has landed on its edge. Noah's 143.1 is his season high and he's 2-6, which for him is roughly on schedule. We had Noah by nine.

copies.headline: Lamar's Zero Hands John The Brotherly Sweep
copies.body:
Peter started a quarterback who scored nothing. That's the whole game in one line — Lamar Jackson posted 0.0 against a 22.2 projection, and even Justin Herbert's miserable 7.8 on the bench would have been infinite improvement. Add Bijan Robinson's 7.6 on a 20.1 projection and George Pickens' 6.8 while Adonai Mitchell dropped 27.2 in street clothes, and Peter left roughly 50 points unplayed in a game he lost by 47.
John didn't need to be clever. Brock Bowers went for 28.2 out of the flex, D'Andre Swift added 27.9, Puka Nacua and Trey McBride cleared 20, and Tyler Bass outscored Peter's entire quarterback and kicker rooms combined. Matthew Stafford's 8.3 was the only soft spot and it never mattered. We had John by 14; he tripled it.
Both sit 5-3, but the underlying numbers aren't close — John's 69% all-play to Peter's 45%, who's been living on +1.4 luck wins. And big brother is now 7-3 all-time.

intro: Isaac survived Adam by 3.9 and Leif edged Kaleb by 1.9 in a game that combined for 127 points, which is less than John put up by himself in a 47-point demolition of Peter. Logan and Noah each cleared 143 to win by better than 33, so the week split cleanly into teams that scored and teams that watched. Leif and Kaleb should probably agree never to speak of it again.
